title: Ninety-second integration ripcord cards (seller ops draft)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working set of ultra-short sales-engineer "ripcord" cards for sellers and SEs to use when an integration pilot is spinning out (latency, cost, or quality surprises) and we need to get to a deterministic next step in under 90s.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Pilots often devolve into long logs + back-and-forth. Customers lose confidence. Sellers lose momentum.
- We need a compact, experiment-first set of checks + scripts + escalation language to: 1) triage quickly, 2) give immediate mitigation options (cheap, reversible), 3) scope a follow-up technical action.

How to use these cards:
- Opening (30s): Ask: "Is this blocking core UX?" If yes, use the Emergency Ripcord. If no, use the Non-blocking triage.
- Speak the script verbatim for consistent handoff.
- After the 90s check, either (A) apply a mitigation and confirm progress, or (B) open a single JIRA ticket and book a 30-min follow-up.

Card A — Emergency ripcord (for blockers):
Quick script: "We need to pause and stabilize. We'll route traffic to a fallback model variant and open a 30-min deep-dive. Expect follow-up in 15 minutes."
Steps (90s):
1) Switch route in playground/console to fallback-model: model-compact-v1 (Console path: Routes > active > edit route > fallback) — note current route in notes.
2) Turn on request-sampling (1%) for full logging only if privacy OK.
3) Notify SRE & SE on Slack channel #pilot-escalations with TL;DR: customer, symptom, step taken, ticket id.
4) Create short ticket (JIRA-OPS-xxxx) with: one-sentence problem, steps we did, sample request id, contact (customer & SE).

Rapid checks (30s diagnostics checklist):
- Is the symptom latency, hallucination, or cost spike? (pick one)
- Any recent model swap/quantize/rollout in the last 24h? (check rollout log)
- Error spike vs. slow tail (p50 vs p99)? Pull last 30m p50/p95/p99 if console available.

Card B — Non-blocking triage (for degraded but usable):
Quick script: "Thanks — this is helpful. We’ll run a short test to reproduce and get back in under an hour. If it’s intermittent we may apply temporary throttles or caching."
Steps (90s):
1) Capture 3 reproducer prompts (ask customer for 2 variants + use one from logs). Save as: repros/customer-<shortid>.
2) Run a local quick-run with model-compact-preview and model-llama-2-mini to compare results. Note delta in outputs.
3) Check cache hit rate for the endpoint (console -> metrics -> cache). If hit rate < 10% and the workload is prefix-heavy, suggest enabling prefix caching.
4) If cost spike, flip quantization to q8_optimized for the route (if quality acceptable).

Script snippets to copy into Slack/email (30s):
- Slack DM to SE: "Opening JIRA-OPS-XXXX: Pilot <customer> experiencing <symptom>. Flipped to fallback-model (model-compact-v1). Need SRE assist for logs + p99 tail. Contact: <se-name>."
- Customer email: "Short update: we saw the issue and routed a safer model variant to stabilize. We're investigating root cause and will reply within 1h with next steps."

Roleplay micro-examples (30s each):
- Seller voice for cost spike: "We can throttle non-critical routes and enable token caps per-request. If you’d like, we can also run a sample of your top-10 prompts through our Optimize tool to surface batching/quantize wins."
- SE voice for hallucination: "Let's grab three failing prompts and run them against the previous model version. If differences persist we escalate to model-onboarding/qa."

Quick technical commands & links (for SEs):
- Check live latency: Console -> Routes -> [route] -> Latency heatmap (last 30m)
- Switch route fallback: Console -> Routes -> Edit -> Fallback model selector
- Temporary token cap: Console -> Request policies -> add per-request limit 256 tokens
- Metric query snippet (copy to metrics UI): "select p95_latency, count(*) from requests where route='customer-abc' and ts>now()-30m"

Decision heuristics (one-liners):
- If p99 > 3x p50 and users report timeouts -> Emergency ripcord.
- If quality regressions affect <5% of requests and are non-critical -> Non-blocking triage + repro set.
- If cost increased by >40% month-over-month for the pilot bucket -> apply quantize+cache and book follow-up.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add small visual quick-reference card for SE Google Slides (size A6) — action: Priya
- Include direct console deep-link generation (API support request) — open JIRA-CLI ticket.
- Need a short one-click email template in Outreach/HubSpot for the stabilized update.

Attachments & evidence to gather post-90s (these are one-line items we drop into the ticket):
- 3x repro prompts + outputs (annotate differences)
- Short metrics snapshot (p50/p95/p99 + error rate)
- Route config snapshot (model, quantization, batching params)

Examples from recent pilots (copied notes):
- Pilot: FinX internal (2026-01-20) — symptom: p99 tail after model swap; action: rolled back last canary, routed to compact model, fixed within 45 mins.
- Pilot: HealthDesk (2025-12-14) — symptom: hallucination with medical-extraction prompt; action: enabled function-calls enforcement + increased safety-filter threshold, then queued a model onboarding ticket.

Communication dos & don’ts (short):
- DO: Use clear, timeboxed language — "we’ll follow up in X minutes/hours".
- DO: Preserve customer context in the ticket (sample prompt + expected output).
- DON’T: Promise long-term fixes in the stabilization message.

Shelf-life and next steps for this doc:
- This is a rapidly iterating playlet. Expected to be used in Q1 2026 pilot ops.
- Next revision: embed console deep-links and add a 1-click HubSpot email.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please add any missing console nav paths that are out-of-date (I had to approximate for some new console UX elements).
- If you've seen a better one-liner that calms customers faster, paste into comments.

End of doc — quick checklist before shipping to SEs:
- [ ] Priya: slide A6 mock for cheat card
- [ ] Evan: standard Slack template + channel naming confirm
- [ ] Tom: open JIRA template with required fields

(Informal + in-progress — expect typos and TODOs. This lives in Drive as the 90s ripcord working copy.)
